name: AURIGA — dark matter searches
full_name: AURIGA cryogenic resonant-mass detector dark-matter searches
summary: A cryogenic resonant-bar gravitational-wave detector repurposed to search for ultralight scalar dark matter that coherently deforms solids.
detection_principle: A Galactic scalar field coupled to ordinary matter may drive a resonant bar at its Compton frequency, producing a narrowband strain peak.

sites.name: INFN Laboratori Nazionali di Legnaro, near Padova
sites.location: INFN Laboratori Nazionali di Legnaro, near Padova

status.label: Historical observing instrument, now on public display
status.evidence: INFN's 2021 report describes AURIGA's history and public display; its dark-matter result was published in 2016.

timeline.event: Search for light scalar Dark Matter candidate with AURIGA detector

collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Assuming a standard halo density of 0.3 GeV/cm³, a 95% CL upper bound of approximately 10⁻⁵ is set on modulus coupling near the representative mass.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
